title: Limit law for tuple multiplicities in random run sequences
summary: Determine the limiting normalized distribution of how often n-tuples occur in a uniformly random binary run sequence.

formal_statement.body: Choose uniformly from the cyclically distinct binary run sequences of period $2^n-1$. For a chosen sequence, let $a_i$ be the number of nonzero $n$-tuples that occur exactly $i$ times, so that $\sum_{i\ge0}a_i=2^n-1$ and $\sum_{i\ge0}i a_i=2^n-1$. Determine the limiting law of the normalized multiplicities $a_i/(2^n-1)$ as $n\to\infty$: prove convergence for every fixed $i$ and characterize the complete limiting probability distribution.

scope.domain: Probability distribution of tuple occurrences in binary pseudorandom run sequences
assumptions: Sampling is uniform over cyclically distinct binary run sequences of period $2^n-1$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The source proves that each fixed nonzero tuple has average occurrence tending to one, but that first-moment statement does not determine the multiplicity distribution. The normalized limit law remains open.

citations.label: Kim--Song, run-sequence enumeration and distribution problems

progress.summary: The source asks for the average occurrence-multiplicity distribution of a random run sequence and states that its normalized large-order limit is wide open.
